Riga's old town is a World Heritage Site. On Midsummer night there's a festival where people sing and dance all night.

nordic:6.fact: The country where Japanese diplomat Sugihara Chiune helped many people.
nordic:6.about:
In 1940, in Kaunas, Lithuania, Japanese diplomat Sugihara Chiune kept writing visas to travel through Japan for many people who had to leave their country. He's said to have saved about 6,000 lives.
They're still remembered as "visas for life," a story that connects Japan and Lithuania.

#western-europe-2: A chocolate country, an Alpine country, a music country. They may be small, but they're full of character.

western-europe-2:0.fact: A country famous around the world for chocolate and waffles.
western-europe-2:0.about:
Belgium is famous for chocolate and waffles, and the Grand-Place, the main square in Brussels, is said to be one of the most beautiful squares in the world.
Dutch is spoken in the north, French in the south and German in part of the east. The headquarters of the EU (European Union) is in Brussels too.

western-europe-2:1.fact: An Alpine country with 4 official languages.
western-europe-2:1.about:
Switzerland is surrounded by the Alps, and it has 4 official languages: German, French, Italian and Romansh.
The Matterhorn, watchmaking and cheese fondue are famous. There are lots of mountain railways, so you can go up to the mountaintops by train.

western-europe-2:2.fact: A music country, where Mozart was born.
western-europe-2:2.about:
Salzburg in Austria is where Mozart was born, and the capital, Vienna, is called "the city of music," where many composers worked.
The Vienna Boys' Choir has more than 500 years of history. "Wiener Schnitzel," a thin piece of meat fried in breadcrumbs, is a famous dish.

western-europe-2:3.fact: One of the homes of Halloween.
western-europe-2:3.about:
Ireland is so green and beautiful that it's called the "Emerald Isle." Halloween grew from old autumn festivals in places like Ireland. The first jack-o'-lanterns were made from turnips.
On St Patrick's Day, March 17th, whole towns turn green. The country's symbol is the harp.

western-europe-2:4.fact: "Pan" (bread) is Portuguese. Castella came from Portugal to Nagasaki too!
western-europe-2:4.about:
About 480 years ago, Portugal was one of the first European countries to come to Japan. Many Japanese words come from Portuguese, like "pan" (bread), "botan" (button) and "kappa" (raincoat).
Castella, konpeitō sweets and tempura are also said to have come from contact with Portugal. It's a country with very deep ties to Nagasaki.

western-europe-2:5.fact: All the buses and trains in the country are free!
western-europe-2:5.about:
Luxembourg is a small country about the size of Kanagawa. In 2020, it became the first country in the world to make all its buses, trains and trams free.
People switch between three languages: Luxembourgish, French and German.

western-europe-2:6.fact: The second-smallest country in the world.
western-europe-2:6.about:
Monaco is the second-smallest country in the world after Vatican City. It's only about 4 times the size of Tokyo Disneyland.
The "Monaco Grand Prix," a car race on the town's own streets, is famous. On cliffs by the sea stand a palace and an aquarium.

#eastern-europe: Castle towns, hot spring towns, a valley of roses. In the middle of Europe are countries like something out of a fairy tale.

eastern-europe:0.fact: The country where Chopin and Marie Curie were born.
eastern-europe:0.about:
Poland is where Chopin, "the poet of the piano," and Marie Curie, who won the Nobel Prize twice, were born. An international piano competition named after Chopin is held in Warsaw.
In the Wieliczka Salt Mine, you can see an underground chapel and statues made of salt.

eastern-europe:1.fact: The word "robot" was born in Czechia.
eastern-europe:1.about:
The word "robot" was first used in 1920 in a play by Czech writer Karel Čapek. It was made from a Czech word meaning "work."
Prague, the capital, has an astronomical clock that has been running since 1410, and every hour little figures start to move.

eastern-europe:2.fact: The home of the Rubik's Cube. People say their family name first, like in Japan!
eastern-europe:2.about:
In Hungary, people say their family name first, just like in Japan. Rubik Ernő, who made the Rubik's Cube, is Hungarian too.
The capital, Budapest, was made by joining the towns of "Buda" and "Pest" on either side of the Danube, and it has lots of hot springs.

eastern-europe:3.fact: Neckties began as the scarves of Croatian soldiers.
eastern-europe:3.about:
In the 17th century, the scarves Croatian soldiers wore around their necks became fashionable in France, and they became the first neckties. The French word for necktie, "cravate," comes from "Croatia."
The town of Dubrovnik, on the Adriatic Sea, is called "the pearl of the Adriatic."

eastern-europe:4.fact: It has monasteries with outside walls covered in paintings.
eastern-europe:4.about:
In the Bukovina region of northern Romania, there are monasteries whose outside walls are covered in painted stories, and they're World Heritage Sites.
The Danube Delta, where the Danube flows into the sea, is one of Europe's great wetlands, home to more than 300 kinds of birds, including pelicans.

eastern-europe:5.fact: Rose oil from the Valley of Roses is world famous.
eastern-europe:5.about:
In Bulgaria's "Valley of Roses," roses are picked in May and June to make rose oil, which is used in perfume. Bulgaria is one of the world's top producers of rose oil.
It's famous for yoghurt too. And in Bulgaria, nodding your head up and down can mean "no," and shaking it from side to side can mean "yes."

eastern-europe:6.fact: About 60% of the country is forest. Lake Bled, with a church on an island, is famous.
eastern-europe:6.about:
Slovenia is a green country, with about 60% of its land covered in forest. A church stands on a little island in Lake Bled, like a picture postcard.
Underground there are lots of big limestone caves, where the olm, a blind salamander, lives.
